sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Vessel Brokerage of Agricultural Soybeans and Yellow Corn

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (based on the Napoleonic Code, with partnership and commercial law codified in the Luxembourg Code of Commerce and Civil Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China BIT (signed 12 June 1985, entered into force 27 August 1986)
Luxembourg–United States FTA (not a bilateral FTA but favorable double taxation avoidance via US-Luxembourg DTT effective 15 December 2000)
Luxembourg Double Taxation Treaties (DTTs) with more than 80 jurisdictions, including France, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, UK, and most OECD jurisdictions
Energy Charter Treaty (for relevant investments; withdrawals pending but treaty remains in force for existing investments)
EU internal market freedoms applicable through the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 27 July 2022 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 27 juillet 2022 portant création d’un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) consolidating the former Law of 13 January 2019. Primary AML legal framework: Law of 23 January 2023 amending the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended), implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD). Secondary guidance from the Luxembourg Banking and Finance Commission (CSSF) Regulation 12-02 and Grand Ducal Regulation of 31 October 2018.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access_with_Restricted_Public_Access (registered with Luxembourg Register of Commercial and Companies (RCS); public access granted to specific legitimate interest holders; authorities, credit institutions, and notaries have full access; the public register allows access to those demonstrating a legitimate interest, subject to data protection restrictions and court redaction orders approved under the law of 27 July 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Statuts / Acte constitutif) of the SCSp authenticated copy for registry filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire) in whose protocol the deed is passed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where origin-issued abroad) or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions; e.g., China, Canada, and others not party to the Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Procuration) for resident manager (initial signatory) or incorporator, if executed outside Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or public authority in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport (or national ID) of each UBO, director, and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority of the respective nationality (e.g., municipal registrar, immigration authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarial certification with consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; translated into French/German/Luxembourgish by a sworn translator if required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address (utility bill, bank statement) for each UBO and manager, dated within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; certified translation if not in French/German/English

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Luxembourg's CSSF AML/CFT benchmarks: (i) OFAC SDN List, (ii) United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, (iii) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (iv) Luxembourg's own national freezing list published by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU - Cellule de renseignement financier, CRF), (v) Interpol Red Notices, and (vi) World Bank Debarment List. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is automatically triggered for politically exposed persons (PEPs) defined as individuals entrusted with prominent public functions domestically, within EU institutions, or in third countries, along with family members and close associates. To comply with the Law of 27 July 2022, the registered agent or notary must verify the true identity of each UBO by obtaining proof of identity, address, and beneficial ownership declarations; moreover, for non-EU PEPs, a higher risk rating and senior management approval is required before advancement of commercial registration. The protocol includes continuous monitoring for negative news, sanctions list updates, and specific FATF high-risk jurisdiction identification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (Luxembourg Business Registers - LBR) electronic platform, managed by the Ministry of Justice and the Luxembourg House of Entrepreneurship; the corporate name reservation is made via the online portal 'MyLBR' or the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) official e-service (www.lbr.lu). The official registry of commercial names is the 'RCS Luxembourg' available online at www.lbr.lu.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in one of Luxembourg's official languages: French, German, or Luxembourgish; however, a Latin script transliteration or a commonly used English name can be accepted provided it respects the legal form designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. Names written in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Cyrillic, Chinese, Arabic) are required to be transliterated into one of the official languages using standard Latin script; no private translations are accepted unless certified by a sworn translator. The name must comply with the principle of 'consistency in the use of language' (Article 25 of the Luxembourg Code of Commerce). For the substantiation of distinguishing character, the name must not be misleading or confusing with existing commercial names, trademarks, or protected appellations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five business days of administrative refusal, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Ministry of Justice, addressing the Registrar of the RCS ('Registre de commerce et des sociétés'). The appeal must include justification of the distinguishing character and, if applicable, documented consent from the holder of a prior registered trade name. If the refusal is based on the use of a sensitive token, the appellant must produce a prior ministerial authorization for that token, otherwise the appeal is likely to be dismissed. The Ministry of Justice must decide within one month; an adverse or silent decision can then be appealed to the Luxembourg administrative tribunal ('Tribunal administratif') within one month of the notification or deemed refusal. No extension of the name reservation validity beyond the 30-day period is available, but a fresh reservation can be requested after the expiry, subject to paying a new filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a pure SCSp operating as a commodity brokerage (ISIC 4631) with no regulated financial activity, a virtual office (i.e., a registered address service provided by an accredited service provider without physical occupancy) is generally permissible, provided the SCSp maintains a registered office with a real street address (not a PO Box) in Luxembourg and a registered agent. The Luxembourg RCS does not require physical on-site staff or premises for a passive partnership; however, a minimum of one shareholder and one general partner (which can be a corporate entity) with a Luxembourg registered office is required. The LBR/corporate law permits the use of a service-provider address (domiciliation), but the provider must be an approved 'domiciliation agent' (agrément) under the law of 31 May 1999. The permissibility may be curtailed if the brokerage activity expands into handling client money or becomes a regulated commodities exchange, but for low-risk standard commercial activity it is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: 10-15% risk per year for standard SCSp entities. The Luxembourg tax authority (Administration des contributions directes) and the commercial registry may request financial statements or conduct off-site document reviews; unannounced physical inspections are generally limited to cases where a reasonable suspicion of money laundering, tax evasion, or false domiciliation is identified through the AML/CFT supervision of the CSSF or the business register. However, the domiciliation agent must undergo periodic CSSF inspections, and its clients' premises may be inspected as part of the agent's regulatory review, imposing a 10% audit probability in the first two years for an active brokerage entity, rising to 20% if the partnership files losses continuously or has non-EU UBOs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name reservation fee (individual request for an SCSp)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Luxembourg-IPSG Ordinance on RCS fees (Administrative price list; approx. EUR 27–30).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (authentic act for SCSp, including articles of association) – drafting and legal review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp; statutory minimum notarial tariff under the Grand-Ducal regulation of 21 June 1994 (scale based on share capital, capped at approx. EUR 1,500 for partnerships but typical market fee for bilingual drafting and translation is USD 3,000).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public so-called 'publication fees' – mandatory legal announcement in the Official Gazette (recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Official Journal / RCS publication service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff as per the law of 19 December 2002 (approx. EUR 45–50).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO/RBE) – filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory flat fee for UBO filing (EUR 14–15) under the Law of 27 July 2022.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization fees for documents issued outside the EU (e.g., UBO passports, proof of address, and Power of Attorney) – average bundle of 3–4 documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Various national authorities in country of document issuance (e.g., Foreign Ministry, consulate, apostille service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International benchmark for Hague Apostille USD 20–100 per document plus consular fees for non-Hague jurisdictions; USD 550 represents an aggregated average for a UBO package of two EU and two non-EU documents subject to consular legalization.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of legal documents into French/German/Luxembourgish by sworn translator (e.g., if non-EU origin evidence is submitted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator officially admitted to the Luxembourg list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing tariff of the Luxembourg association of translators (approx. USD 35–50 per page; assuming 10 pages).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service provider fee (annual) – accredited domiciliation agent (for SCSp in commercial sector)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited domiciliation provider (e.g., law firm or corporate service provider approved by the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: annual domiciliation fees range from USD 1,200 to 2,000 for a low-risk SCSp; USD 1,600 is a mid-range quote.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate law counsel fees for due diligence drafting, UBO analysis, and consultation (pre-incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Lawyer (at least a Luxembourg bar 'avocat à la Cour')
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for specialized corporate counsel, typically USD 350–450 per hour; USD 2,500 estimated for 6–8 hours including advice on SCSp commercial viability and AML compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening software / database access for UBO verification (pre-incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party screening provider (e.g., LexisNexis, World-Check, Dow Jones) or outsourcing to counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a one-time due diligence bundle screening (UBO name check and negative news search).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Standard courier/shipping for apostilled originals to Luxembourg (for non-EU UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market price for expedited, tracked document shipment from the UBO's country; USD 100 is an average international envelope rate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Art. 101-137 (limited partnership regime) and Art. 103-1 et seq. (Société en Commandite Spéciale, introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); implemented with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the amended Law of 11 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), National Registry Department, Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société (SCSp partnership deed / articles of association), executed by private deed or notarial deed and submitted to the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital; SCSp is exempt from legal capital requirements. No escrow account is required. Capital consists of free contributions (cash, in-kind, or future supplies) freely fixed in the partnership deed and fully subscribed by the special partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital contributions subscribed by the special partners, as listed in the contribution schedule, are accepted and credited in full, it being recorded that no minimum statutory capital applies to the SCSp. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is adopted at [No.], [Street], L-[City], Luxembourg. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name], acting as manager of the general partner, is appointed sole officer and authorized sole signatory, empowered to file the articles of association with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to arrange RESA publication, and to open and operate bank accounts of the partnership in connection with the bulk grain brokerage business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting in person or through counsel; notary optional unless real estate is contributed (Luxembourg notariat)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the contrat de société containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate object limited to ISIC 4631 bulk grain and oilseed brokerage, identity of the general partner and special partners, contribution schedule, profit-allocation and management provisions. Execute the deed by all partners in original written form. If a corporate general partner is appointed, annex its constitutive documents and evidence of authority. If any contribution consists of real estate, the deed must be notarized by a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Draft SCSp partnership deed (contrat de société)
Certified copies of identity documents of all natural-person partners (passport or national ID)
Extract of civil status records for natural persons
Constitutive deed and current registration extract of any corporate general partner
Power of attorney for each representative signing on behalf of a non-resident partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any defect or inconsistency in the deed by a supplementary corrective deed signed by all partners before submission to the RCS; foreign signatures must be legalized or apostilled and defective mandates replaced before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, online portal www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The appointed manager files the executed partnership deed through the LBR online portal using a qualified electronic signature (LuxTrust). Pay the electronic filing fee and submit the statutory annexes. The registry issues the RCS certificate and extract bearing the partnership registration number and the Luxembourg business identification number.
required_dossiers: Executed SCSp partnership deed
Statement of commencement of business or non-activity declaration
Contribution report or bank confirmation, if cash contributions are stated
LuxTrust qualified electronic signature certificate of the filer
Completed LBR cover sheet (formulaire de demande d'inscription)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registrar raises a priority query, the filer corrects the manifest omission within one month through the LBR portal; if unduly refused, counsel files a formal objection with the registrar and, where necessary, the President of the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) operated by LBR; Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) under the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry publishes the deed in the RESA, the electronic official gazette for companies, conferring opposability to third parties. Concurrently, within one month of registration, submit the RBE declaration through the secure RBE portal, disclosing the natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control the SCSp, with exact ownership percentages and control characterization.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Organizational chart of the ownership chain of the SCSp
Beneficial-owner schedule (name, nationality, date of birth, residential address, nature and percentage of control)
Copy of the profit-sharing clauses of the partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication contains a material error, request correction from LBR in writing and publish the corrected extract. If the RBE issues a contradiction notice, respond within 7 calendar days; failure may lead to transfer to the Public Prosecutor's Office, and a late-filing fine up to EUR 1,250 may be imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national registration number (matricule) at the CCSS and file the VAT liability declaration (Form 13) with the AEDT. Although the SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes, it obtains its own VAT identification number for invoicing brokerage commissions on international grain trade. If employees will be hired, complete the CCSS employer-registration dossier within eight days of the first engagement.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration and extract
VAT registration Form 13 (identification of taxable person)
CCSS entity identification form (CEDTAP / matricule application)
Lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney to any tax adviser or fiscal agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT disputes the place of supply of cross-border brokerage services, submit a written clarification request; the taxpayer may appeal the director's decision of the AEDT within three months. Any CCSS classification question is cured by submitting the employment contracts and payroll projection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME et de l'Entrepreneuriat, Guichet unique (www.guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a written activity description confirming that the SCSp's object is confined to vessel brokerage and intermediation of bulk soybeans and yellow corn, with no physical receipt, storage, processing, or retail of goods at any Luxembourg site. Obtain an administrative acknowledgment confirming that no autorisation d'établissement is required under the amended Law of 2 September 2011, since pure commercial brokerage is not a regulated craft, retail trade, or physical industrial activity.
required_dossiers: Written activity description statement
Extract of the corporate-object clause from the partnership deed
RCS registration extract
Declaration that no warehouse, silo, or processing facility is operated in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry recharacterizes the activity as a regulated trader activity, the general partner must apply for the autorisation d'établissement within 15 days; the permit is issued following checks of good repute and professional competence, and a refusal is appealable before the administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for this pure brokerage scope; reference Guichet unique of the Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale des PME et de l'Entrepreneuriat, which confirms that no industrial operating permit is imposed on ISIC 4631 intermediation activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license is required; the SCSp's business activity is limited to contract intermediation and brokerage of bulk agricultural commodities, so no industrial site authorization, warehouse permit, or grain-handling license applies

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not subject to EIA screening - no physical project, construction, land disturbance, or waste-generating installation is undertaken by the SCSp; office-based commercialization and brokerage fall outside the classes of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; zero process discharge and zero VOC emissions. The registered office remains subject to municipal wastewater ordinances (règlement communal) and the general obligation to segregate office waste under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection certificate for the registered office issued by the competent fire and rescue authority (Service d'Incendie et de Sauvetage) covering evacuation routes and extinguishing equipment; structural and legal-use compliance certificate for the leased office premises; occupational health-and-safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workstations, electrical installations, and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT matters. Primary digital pan-Luxembourg portal: myGuichet (https://myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident economic actor registering for Luxembourg tax purposes must first appoint a Luxembourg fiscal domicile representative or agent in accordance with Arts. 155 and 156 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) and Art. 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (LTVL). For VAT, the foreign entity files a pre-registration dossier with the AEDT through myGuichet or by paper, providing the statutory incorporation deed, balance sheet or forecast turnover statement, a description of the business activities to be performed in Luxembourg, and the national identifier of the foreign enterprise. The AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) and, where a permanent establishment arises, a separate direct-tax registration number is enforced by ACD. The SCSp itself is not registered for corporate income tax where fiscally transparent; instead, its partners report their allocable shares.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is, by operation of law, fiscally transparent; it is not itself a corporate income taxpayer. No generic check-the-box election exists. However, the agreement of the partners may expressly provide that the SCSp carries on a commercial activity and, if the structure falls within the scope of Art. 175 LIR (which requires a legal-personality company with full liability shareholders), tax transparency is excluded and the entity becomes opaque. For cross-border hybrid mismatch purposes, the tax classification of the SCSp must be documented under the Luxembourg ATAD/MLI implementation, and an election to align or reclassify the entity may be filed with the Luxembourg tax administration within the statutory filing window of the annual partnership return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-established taxable persons, no EUR threshold applies and registration is compulsory as from the first taxable supply or acquisition in Luxembourg. Resident small undertakings enjoy a GBP/EUR annual turnover exemption up to EUR 35,000 (Article 169 LTVL) unless conducting export, intra-community or distance-selling transactions. The special EU pan-European distance-sales threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year. Bulk grain, soybean, and corn export transactions from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations are not counted against the domestic threshold and always trigger full registration rights.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time tax clearance or transaction-level digital stamping is currently enacted in Luxembourg for B2B commercial supplies. E-invoicing is mandatory only for domestic public procurement through the ePEK platform. For export zero-rating, the taxable person must issue an invoice under Article 232 of the EU VAT Directive as implemented by the LTVL, maintain an invoice numbering sequence, include the mandatory indication of the 0% rate and the export dispatch and customs declaration numbers, and file the periodic VAT return by the statutory deadline (monthly or quarterly). The Luxembourg VAT returns are submitted electronically through myGuichet; VAT payment, Portuguese, and cancellation of exports are processed via the AEDT, with no gateway API obligation other than the application-to-application reporting in the myGuichet secure channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate is available only where the bulk agricultural commodities are physically dispatched or transported by the supplier or a third party on behalf of the supplier to a destination outside the EU, ownership has transferred to the purchaser, and the supplier holds full documentary proof of dispatch/transport and customs export clearance. Offshore services and maritime vessel brokerage fees linked to the grain trade are zero-rated only where the supply falls under Article 146 VAT Directive, the services relate to goods destined for export, the customer is outside the EU, and the relevant B/L or customs certificate substantiates the offshore use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX1, electronic export summary accepted via Luxembourg PDS/Douane system)
Transport Documents — Bill of Lading, CMR, or multimodal transport document covering the export movement
Commercial invoice and purchase order with Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT wire proof demonstrating receipt of export proceeds
Warehouse or silo/dispatch evidence (weighbridge certificates, export inspection certificate) establishing the exact shipped quantity of soybeans/corn
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to stringent tax administration and customs post-clearance audits. If documentary proof is missing, incomplete, or internally contradictory at the time of audit, AEDT will withdraw the zero rate and assess VAT at 17% on the invoice amount. The assessment carries late-payment interest of 0.6% per month or part thereof, a civil administrative penalty of up to 10% of the tax at issue, and a 5% surcharge for late filing where applicable. Fraudulent simulation of exports, document falsification, or shareholder-linked offshore shell recipients will trigger criminal sanctions under Articles 900 to 911 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law, including monetary fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of responsible directors, together with an unlimited retrospective reopening (limitation suspended during criminal investigation). The clawback period is twenty years where fraud is established and ten years in cases of gross negligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for the banking supervision of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility on both the current and capital accounts pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the euro-area legislative framework. No exchange controls, settlement licensing, or prior-authorisation regimes apply to trade-related payments, investment flows, or profit remittances. The Luxembourg SCSp may freely receive, hold, and disburse USD, EUR, CNY, and all other freely convertible currencies through licensed credit institutions; the sole profit-remittance hurdles are exogenous tax-documentary requirements (e.g., EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, Luxembourg dividend withholding tax of 15% on taxable corporate vehicles, and CRS/FATCA reporting), which bind exclusively in the compliance layer rather than the FX regulatory layer. Capital account repatriation of liquidation proceeds or return of capital is unrestricted, subject only to AML/KYC verification of the beneficial owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no holding-period constraints on export receipts derived from bulk grain, soybean, or corn shipments. Export proceeds may remain indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts at a Luxembourg or EEA-authorised bank and may be applied directly to pay for ocean freight, warehouse charges, or new inventory without any BCL conversion requirement. The only affirmative duty is statistical: resident entities must report cross-border flows to the BCL through the balance-of-payments monthly return (export of goods code 100-level transaction classification, or the applicable direct-investment/trade advance code) and must preserve the underlying contract of sale and shipping documents for inspection by the BCL/CSSF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (compte à vue)
Operational Current Account / Trade Finance and Documentary Credit Facility / Collateral Cash Account
Capital Escrow Account / Multi-currency Settlement Account (EUR-USD-CNY)
Operational Account / Structured Commodity Finance Cash Management Account / LC Backing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. EEA-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) passported into Luxembourg under the Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2) and supervised by the CSSF may lawfully open payment accounts for an SCSp without a domestic banking licence; however, they cannot extend credit, cannot issue Irrevocable Transferable Letters of Credit, and their maximum transaction thresholds commonly truncate bulk-vessel settlements. The SCSp should therefore limit EMI use to ancillary disbursements such as demurrage, survey fees, and small balancing payments. Legal constraint: the EMI must hold the SCSp's e-money float in segregated safeguarded accounts, all funds must pass a full AML/KYC screening identical to that of a universal bank, and any financial intermediation signal will create a presumption of shadow-banking that the SCSp must rebut with an independent legal opinion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for a non-resident SCSp engaged in agricultural commodities. Luxembourg tier-1 credit institutions uniformly require at least one in-person interview at their premises in the Grand Duchy with the general partner (commandité) or a duly authorised senior signatory before account activation. CSSF circular 20/725 and the eIDAS regulation formally permit remote onboarding via qualified video-identification and qualified electronic signatures, and pure remote opening is available only to clients demonstrably presenting minimal AML risk; in the present grain-export structure, with non-resident limited partners and a pass-through partnership, the practical standard is a physical meeting plus certified notarised copies of the deed and partnership agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the ultimate beneficial ownership chain: an SCSp with no minimum capital and a two-tier partnership structure triggers the bank's substantive UBO-identification review under CSSF regulation of 11 January 2019
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement; certificate of registration of the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); UBO declaration lodged with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); signed organisational chart identifying each limited partner above the 25% threshold; a Luxembourg-law legal opinion confirming the pass-through status of the SCSp; audited opening balance sheet or capital call records signed by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure arising from voyage routing through Black Sea, Baltic, or third-country ports of the bulk grain trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete charter-party and bill-of-lading set; vessel IMO voyage log with GPS track; GAFTA or FOSFA conformity certificates; EU, OFAC, and UN sanctions-screening clearance reports; comprehensive end-user undertaking and contractual destination address clauses; statement of origin for the soybean and yellow corn cargoes from the commodity desk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, PEP status, or politically exposed persons associated with the general partner or limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent negative-media screening reports (World-Check or equivalent); source-of-wealth statement supported by personal tax returns and audited financial statements; two independent bank references from institutions of equal tier; an external legal opinion on the reputational standing of each principal; engagement statement of the Luxembourg corporate service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency on capital injections into a pass-through entity without a share capital requirement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Issued capital call notices signed by the general partner; bank account transcripts of the limited partners evidencing the remittance trail; copy of the underlying USD/EUR forward or spot FX booking with the remitting bank; audited or reviewed annual accounts of the contributors; confirmation letter from the fund administrator or domiciliation agent acting in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk of misclassification of commercial activity as regulated financial services requiring a MiFID licence or PSD2 authorisation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised business-plan declaration confined to ISIC 4631 wholesale brokerage and trading of agricultural bulk commodities; sample sales confirmation and standard-form carriage contract; Luxembourg-law legal opinion confirming that the SCSp engages in no payment-instrument issuance, no credit taking, no depositaking, and no trading for third parties; optional written comfort letter from the CSSF submitted by the relationship manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection protocol: (i) all shareholder/partner capital contributions adhere to SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with strict reference to the notarised capital call letter and the SCSp's RCS registration number; (ii) for USD inflows, settlement is cleared via Fedwire/CHIPS through a tier-1 correspondent, and for EUR inflows via TARGET2/SEPA; (iii) the BCL balance-of-payments monthly statistical return codes the transaction as foreign direct investment equity in an investment vehicle (advanced economy code applicable to direct-investment shares in a Luxembourg holding), the general partner must retain the original credit notification; (iv) the bank applies a two-stage verification: first, an OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screen on the remitter, the intermediary, and the beneficiary; second, a purpose-code verification comparing the narrative field of the MT103 against the underlying subscription certificate; (v) no cash or bearer-transfer injections are permitted, every inbound capital flight must be traceable to a regulated banking institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are: SWIFT MT103/MT202 for settlement of grain invoices, demurrage, freight, and insurance premia; irrevocable and transferable documentary Letters of Credit issued and confirmed under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for the purchase contracts of soybean cargoes; and documentary collections under URC 522 (D/P and D/A) as a standby mechanism. For EUR payments, liquidation occurs through TARGET2; for USD payments, through the correspondent banking network via Fedwire/CHIPS with clearly marked commodity-trade purpose code; for CNY and BRL legs, settlement runs through a top-tier correspondent bank under the Chinese (CIPS/SWIFT CNY) and Brazilian (SISBACO) arrangements. The SCSp must maintain pre-negotiated unutilised credit limits at its relationship bank before drawing the LC; every outgoing instruction must be supported by the sales contract, the final invoice, and the bill of lading number to satisfy Article 5 of UCP 600 and the bank's trade-finance compliance programme.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) booked over-the-counter with the relationship bank or a G-20 authorised broker-dealer
FX swap (swap points) for short-term liquidity transformation between the SCSp's USD inflow dates and EUR disbursement dates

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on the Brazilian real (BRL), Indian rupee (INR), Argentine peso (ARS), and Ukrainian hryvnia (UAH) for grain invoice legs where the local currency is non-convertible on delivery
Cross-currency basis swap (EUR/USD) tenor-matched to the underlying working-capital finance facility
FX option package, including zero-cost collars and participation forwards, to hedge the seasonal volatility of soybean and corn price-linked cash flows
Commodity-linked FX forward (dual-currency instrument) structured by the relationship bank for simultaneous commodity price and exchange-rate risk transfer

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg-City aggregate: 17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 95% exemption on qualifying dividends and realized gains from qualifying holdings (10% or EUR 1.2M acquisition threshold, 12-month holding); IP box regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income producing an effective rate of approx. 5.2%; R&D tax credit for eligible research investments; for a transparent SCSp these incentives generally apply at the partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry; no carryback is permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 851 (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, including the municipal business tax section); filed through the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal MyGuichet.lu / e-Tax of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD). For the fiscally transparent SCSp, a pro-forma return of results and partner allocation schedule is attached to the 851.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax year is the calendar year. The return for tax year Y must be filed by 31 December of Y+1 (e.g., FY ending 31 December 2025 is due 31 December 2026). The ACD may grant an extension upon written request; no automatic extension is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal name, RCS registration number, registered office, UBO register number, tax representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg UBO and tax ID of the SCSp; list all non-resident partners with residence state and local tax ID; appoint a Luxembourg tax representative if no local office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross commercial revenue from ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424510 activity: vessel brokerage commissions, freight and demurrage income, LC discount pass-through, ancillary grain handling margins.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source business income and the share attributable to the SCSp’s Luxembourg permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source trading if not connected to Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: charter hire, port costs, shipbrokerage fees, LC and SWIFT bank charges, logistics and IT systems, employee compensation, and allocated overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support each deduction with contemporaneous invoices and bank records; cross-border related-party payments must satisfy arm’s length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable operating profit before incentives and allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile book profit with tax profit; for agri-commodity brokerage, maintain a consistent net margin benchmark and transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income to each partner in accordance with the SCSp agreement (transparency principle).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule showing each partner’s name, residence, profit-share percentage, and allocated amount; non-resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg on the allocated Luxembourg PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) computation and Luxembourg-City rate (6.75%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp itself is generally subject to municipal business tax even when fiscally transparent; declare the Luxembourg PE local-book profit and apply the commune rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Incentive and relief section: participation exemption, IP box deduction, foreign tax credits, and treaty-relief claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 22 / tax residence certificate (TRC) for treaty claims; flow-through deductions are reported on the partner schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the tax assessed (minimum EUR 50) plus monthly late-payment interest of approximately 0.6% (7.2% per annum). If no return is filed after formal notice, the ACD issues an estimated assessment and may impose coercive daily fines (astreinte); deliberate non-filing is prosecuted as tax fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% is the standard Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a capital company. However, the SCSp is a transparent partnership and its periodic profit allocations are not legal dividends; thus Luxembourg does not impose dividend withholding tax on SCSp distributions. If an SCSp is recharacterized as opaque under a foreign treaty or domestic reconstruction, relief may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on dividends or items recharacterized as dividends, the recipient partner must obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and file it with the Luxembourg ACD or the paying agent before payment using Form 22 / 22LB. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, evidence of 12-month beneficial holding and legal form is required. For SCSp business income, non-resident partners claim treaty relief on the PE profits through Luxembourg filing, not through withholding: the residence country grants exemption or credit under the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties (0% statutory rate). Treaty rates only matter in the foreign recipient state and in the source state if the foreign jurisdiction imposes WHT on payments to Luxembourg. Inbound interest/royalty paid to the SCSp may be subject to foreign WHT at treaty rates (commonly 0%, 5%, or 10%), creditable against Luxembourg tax at partner level.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 (group consolidated revenue threshold under the EU CbCR / Master File / Local File regime); below that threshold, Luxembourg ACD may still require contemporaneous TP documentation for all related-party commodity transactions where annual related-party turnover exceeds EUR 2,000,000 or where the profit margin of the SCSp is outside an arm’s length range.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations modeled on the UAE/Guernsey regimes; however, domestic GAAR (LIR § 6, Steueranpassungsgesetz) and EU anti-abuse law impose substantive requirements. An SCSp conducting bulk grain and soybean/corn brokerage must maintain a physical office, local management with genuine decision-making authority, adequate staff and expenses proportionate to turnover, and an actual commercial risk profile. A letter-box SCSp will lose treaty and EU directive benefits and be recharacterized as an abusive conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Luxembourg-source brokerage commissions and charter income from the annual Form 851; creation of fictitious vessel charter invoices routed to low-tax related companies; off-book kickback payments in bulk grain trades.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Comprehensive administrative reassessment of all omitted income; fraud penalties up to 50% of evaded tax plus late-payment interest; criminal fine of up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO §§ 397 et seq.); attachment and seizure of bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of an SCSp and its managers are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, penalties, and interest; criminal conviction may lead to imprisonment up to 5 years, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and disqualification from serving as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp solely as a mailbox and conduit to transfer grain-trading margins into a low-tax offshore LP; no decision-making or staff in Luxembourg; no local books are maintained; the Luxembourg entity does not genuinely control vessel chartering or contractual risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg tax treaty benefits, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, and domestic participation exemption; full recharacterization of revenues as Luxembourg taxable income; GAAR adjustment plus default interest; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 and possible 10% penalty on additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner may be ordered to pay the recovered tax and damages; personal forfeiture orders; travel bans during criminal investigation; imprisonment for intentional sham-arrangement conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer due diligence on counterparties and ultimate beneficial owners of bulk-vessel charters; processing SWIFT wires from sanctioned ports or suspicious grain traders; using bearer-share or nominee arrangements; ignoring OFAC/EU sanctions referrals on soybean and corn shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for AML breaches; criminal money-laundering penalties of up to 5 years’ imprisonment and fine up to EUR 500,000; confiscation of trade proceeds; suspension of operations for repeat violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, managers, and the general partner face personal fines and criminal prosecution; professional debarment from financial services; travel bans; personal seizure of assets; imprisonment up to 5 years for laundering grain-commodity funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the Luxembourg TP documentation for related-party grain procurement and chartering arrangements; allocating more than 10% of the arm’s length trading margin to a non-substantiated low-tax affiliate; not maintaining CUP, cost, or TNMM benchmarks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm’s length upward adjustment of Luxembourg taxable income; late-payment interest; penalty of 10% of the adjustment (up to EUR 25,000); extension of the statute of limitations on tax assessments; refusal of loss compensation and foreign tax credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false TP declarations are jointly and severally liable for the understated tax; criminal sanctions follow if false documents are provided to the ACD; travel bans and personal financial restitution may be ordered.
